summary.one_liner: Built a Redis-backed rate limiter middleware for the Express API to prevent abuse on the /auth endpoints
summary.problem_statement: The /auth/login and /auth/register endpoints were being hit by credential-stuffing bots, causing elevated DB load and occasional lockouts for real users
summary.approach: Implemented a sliding-window rate limiter using Redis ZADD/ZRANGEBYSCORE. Each request adds a timestamped entry to a per-IP sorted set; requests older than the window are pruned atomically. If count exceeds the limit, return 429 with a Retry-After header. Wrapped as Express middleware so any route can opt in with a single line.

tradeoffs.reasoning: Fixed windows allow burst at the boundary (e.g. 100 req at :59 + 100 req at :01). Sliding window is smoother and harder to game.
tradeoffs.alternative_considered: Fixed window counter with Redis INCR+EXPIRE — simpler but vulnerable to boundary bursts

tradeoffs.reasoning: In-memory state is not shared across Node.js worker processes or multiple API instances behind a load balancer
tradeoffs.alternative_considered: express-rate-limit with MemoryStore — fine for single-process, breaks in prod cluster

dead_ends: Tried using a Lua script for atomicity but hit a Redis cluster key-slot constraint — fell back to a pipeline with WATCH/MULTI/EXEC
Initially used Date.now() for timestamps but switched to Redis TIME command to avoid clock skew between app servers
